source_verification_receipts.locator: Definition 3.1 and Theorems 3.2--3.3; Section 3.1, lines 251--341 and 347--353
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines scaled inverse-propensity convergence, proves marginal and joint deterministic Gaussian IPW-Z limits with a consistent sandwich estimator, and gives a clipped no-intercept LinUCB numerical example with two self-reinforcing modes and non-normal IPW-Z behavior.

The paper introduces target-specific directional stability, explicitly contrasts it with full-matrix stability, and derives asymptotic normality and efficiency for scalar targets under that condition.

The paper studies generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, obtains SDE-invariant-law behavior for multiple optimal arms, and develops Gaussian versus non-Gaussian adaptive-inference limits for normalized arm means.
The paper targets an off-policy projected solution under a stationary evaluation policy and uses time-varying flexible variance stabilization to permit unstable or nonconvergent logging policies.
The article studies lock-in probabilities for stochastic approximation with finitely many candidate limit points and bounds convergence to a prescribed point conditional on its attraction domain.
The article treats rates in martingale CLTs through normalized quadratic variation and Lindeberg conditions, including bounded-increment martingales.
The paper proves identifiability for finite mixtures of normal distributions, supporting the scalar every-level mixture-identification step.
The article defines causal excursion effects for micro-randomized trials and uses HeartSteps as a motivating digital-intervention application.
The paper studies pooled longitudinal adaptive sampling with a growing number of users, Z-estimation, and an adaptive sandwich estimator for dependence induced by pooled learning.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a corollary that states the finite-basin mixture and fixed-sandwich frontier directly for a named scalar causal excursion-effect score, including the exact score and contrast used by a HeartSteps-style deployment.

Provide a non-artificial finite-attractor policy family, beyond the one-step-locking witness, for which the attraction modulus is proved and the realized-QV pivot can be instantiated without relying on the unresolved Guo--Xu dynamics question.

State an explicit uniform Kolmogorov-error bound for the realized-QV pivot in terms of T, r_T, and delta_T, rather than only convergence, to make the strict upgrade over the pointwise comparator operational.
